episodes.description: Diogo Almeida is the Co-Founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI, the company behind Jev. Jev is an AI model that lets software make decisions automatically and tells developers how confident it is in each call. According to Sequoia's Pat Grady, it went from zero to $100M in revenue in seven days. TypeSafe's latest round valued the company at $7.5BN, with Martin Casado at Andreessen Horowitz leading and Sequoia also investing. Before TypeSafe, Diogo was a researcher at OpenAI, where he helped invent ChatGPT. episodes.title: Paul Christiano – We could be 12 months away from AIs that can overthrow the government
episodes.description: Paul Christiano is head of the Alignment Research Center. Previously, he was head of AI safety at the US AI Safety Institute. Before that, he led alignment at OpenAI, where he invented RLHF. He’s recently joined OpenAI’s board (though here he is speaking as a private citizen). Paul thinks that on the current trajectory (absent any slowing down), there is a 1 in 3 chance that we could have superintelligence powerful enough to overthrow the government within a year. (He articulates a concrete scenario). He argues that the labs should pause further algorithmic progress until they can secure their weights and research secrets. episodes.title: How an American AI Company Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models
episodes.description: This week, we got news that the Trump administration is reportedly considering a requirement for US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models. Any effort to discourage US businesses from using Chinese open-source could be a big deal for both the AI industry and the market, where investors are still debating whether customers will ultimately be willing to pay for pricier homegrown frontier models versus cheaper alternatives. Everyone remembers last year's 'DeepSeek moment' for AI, when a Chinese company released a cheaper model that seemed nearly as good as cutting-edge US ones. episodes.description: It has been a historic week for AI: the Anthropic IPO and the ongoing situation at Nvidia headline a pretty head-spinning time for the industry. Despite Nvidia's earnings outlook looking good, and despite the scale of the Anthropic IPO — it's oversubscribed, as you might know — there are so many open questions about the state of the industry right now. Today's episode is a special two-parter that addresses some of these questions. episodes.title: How GTA VI Became the Most Expensive Video Game Ever Made
episodes.description: It took over a decade to make Grand Theft Auto VI . And when it's released on November 19, it will have likely already set at least one record: the most expensive video game ever made. In the years since the last GTA release, the video game industry has changed massively. Investors, once excited by the prospect of blockbuster video games, have pulled back, sales have stagnated, and the industry as a whole seems more precarious. Bloomberg News video game reporter Jason Schreier has been following Rockstar Games and its quest to release GTA VI for a long time. episodes.title: The Impossible Trilemma That Hangs Over the Nvidia Crisis
episodes.description: Tian Yang, CIO and manager of the VPX fund at Variant Perception, recently published a report called The Sovereign Impossible Trinity that is especially salient right now. Yang's thesis is that the US-China rivalry is exposing three main policy trade-offs: The necessity of sovereignty (which both of the great powers insist on) means that neither state can assure they can maintain the trio of guns (or the AI 'arms race'), butter (social spending), and sound money because of physical constraints, political conditions, and inflation. episodes.title: How Wall Street Is Bracing For the Post-Jensen Huang Nvidia Era
episodes.description: Nvidia's post-Jensen Huang era has just begun and there are so many open questions about the company's future. Who will the board choose to be Nvidia's next CEO? Will the government crack down on the chipmaker's business practices, particularly in Asia? And will Nvidia's uncertain position begin to spillover into the wider AI ecosystem, from the labs to data center providers? Stacy Rasgon, managing director and senior analyst at Bernstein, isn't optimistic about the short term future of Nvidia and he talks to us today about the cloudy outlook at the company in the wake of Jensen's resignation. We also discuss why he chose to downgrade Nvidia's stock, the surreal experience of covering Jensen's fall as an analyst, and what he's paying attention to ahead of Nvidia's earnings.
